v.q: Which question does distributed tracing answer that metrics and logs alone do not?
o: Where did the time go in this one request across all services?
How many requests per second does the cluster handle?
What is the heap size of each pod?
v.w: Metrics aggregate and logs are per service; a trace follows one request end to end.

v.q: Which chain of signals is the usual way to investigate a slowdown?
o: Metric alert, example trace, slow span, logs of that span
Logs, then a restart, then metrics
Trace, then a redeploy, then logs
v.w: The trace ID links the signals.

v.q: What is a span?
o: One timed operation with a name, start, end, status and attributes
The whole journey of one request
A header that carries the context
v.w: A trace is the tree of spans of one request.

v.q: What do all spans of one trace share?
v.w: Each span has its own span ID and points to its parent.

v.q: A service calls another over HTTP. Which spans are created?
o: A CLIENT span in the caller and a SERVER span in the callee
A PRODUCER and a CONSUMER span
v.w: The gap between them is network and queueing time.

v.q: Which span kinds describe sending and receiving a message?
v.w: They continue the trace across a broker.

v.q: What does the W3C traceparent header contain?
o: Version, trace ID, parent span ID and flags
v.w: For example 00-<32 hex trace id>-<16 hex span id>-01.

v.q: What does the flags field 01 in traceparent mean?
o: The trace is the first of the day
v.w: The head-sampling decision travels downstream with it.

v.q: What is baggage?
o: Your own key-values propagated to every service in the trace
The size limit of a span
v.w: It is sent in headers to every callee.

v.q: Why must baggage never carry secrets or personal data?
o: It is sent in headers to every service called, including third parties
It is deleted after one hop
It is only stored in logs
v.w: Use identifiers only.

v.q: A trace stops at one service and the rest is a separate trace. What is a likely cause?
o: The HTTP client was built with new RestTemplate(), so no traceparent header was sent
The trace ID is too long
v.w: Use the auto-configured builders so the client is instrumented.

v.q: Which hop commonly loses the context?
o: A thread pool or reactive chain without context propagation
v.w: The same problem as the MDC.

v.q: What does OpenTelemetry provide?
o: Vendor-neutral APIs, SDKs, the OTLP protocol, semantic conventions and the Collector
A tracing backend with a UI
v.w: Backends such as Jaeger or Tempo store and show the data.

v.q: Which resource attribute identifies the service in every span?
v.w: Without it spans appear as unknown_service.

v.q: What are the stages of an OpenTelemetry Collector pipeline?
o: Inputs, filters and outputs of the JVM
v.w: Applications send OTLP to the receiver.

v.q: Why put a Collector between services and the backend?
o: It batches, retries, samples, scrubs and routes, so the backend can change without redeploying services
It makes spans smaller than one byte
It replaces the SDK in every service
It removes the need for sampling
v.w: It also centralises sampling and attribute scrubbing.

v.q: Which dependencies give a Spring Boot 3 service OpenTelemetry tracing over OTLP?
v.w: Sleuth ended with Spring Boot 2.

v.q: Which property sets the share of traces sampled in Spring Boot?
v.w: The default is 0.1.

v.q: Which HTTP client is instrumented automatically in Spring Boot 3?
o: One created from RestClient.Builder or RestTemplateBuilder
A raw java.net.http.HttpClient built by hand
A client created with a static factory
v.w: Only clients built from the auto-configured builders get the observation.

v.q: Which settings turn on tracing for Kafka in Spring Boot?
v.w: The context travels in record headers.

v.q: What is an advantage of the OpenTelemetry Java agent?
o: Zero-code instrumentation of many libraries, useful for legacy services
It removes the need for a backend
v.w: Run it with -javaagent.

v.q: What is wrong with running the Java agent and Micrometer Tracing in one service?
v.w: Choose one.

v.q: What is the weakness of head-based sampling?
o: It decides before the outcome is known, so rare errors and slow traces may be dropped
It needs a lot of memory in the Collector
v.w: At 1 percent, 99 percent of failing requests are dropped too.

v.q: How does a downstream service learn the head-sampling decision?
o: From the sampled flag in traceparent
v.w: That keeps a trace whole or absent.

v.q: What does tail-based sampling need that head-based does not?
o: Buffering whole traces and sending all spans of a trace to the same Collector
v.w: Use a load-balancing exporter keyed by trace ID.

v.q: Which tail policies keep the valuable traces?
o: Keep all errors, all slow traces, and a small baseline of the rest
Keep only traces that start on Monday
v.w: The status_code, latency and probabilistic policies.

v.q: In a waterfall, 40 identical SELECT spans in a row point to what?
v.w: Visible mainly in traces.

v.q: A big gap between a CLIENT span and its SERVER span means what?
o: Network or queueing delay, not the callee's own code
The callee has a bug in its SQL
v.w: Look at thread pools and connection queues.

v.q: How does a log line connect to a trace?
o: The trace ID and span ID are put in the MDC and printed on every line
The log file is named after the trace
Logs are stored inside the span
The logger calls the trace backend
v.w: %X{traceId} in the pattern.

v.q: What is an exemplar?
o: A trace ID attached to a metric bucket so a spike links to a real trace
A copy of a log file
v.w: It closes the loop from metric to trace.

v.q: Which span name has the right cardinality?
v.w: Use route templates, never real identifiers.

v.q: Which must never be stored in a span attribute?
o: A password, token or full card number
v.w: Spans go to a shared backend readable by many people.

v.q: A child span seems to start before its parent. What is the likely cause?
o: A bug in the trace ID
v.w: Run NTP or chrony on every node.

v.q: How should you read durations across hosts?
o: Trust durations inside one service and the parent-child structure more than absolute cross-host timestamps
v.w: Small cross-host differences are noise.
